gen-fs-quilon-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Anek Gurmukhi keeps its rounds generous and open, a plain sans with no fuss. Quilon leads with the softly tilted-nib variation of a display face, while Anek Gurmukhi does the quieter job of staying clear and steady line after line.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-anek-latin: Quilon looks editorial and sure of itself. Its strokes swell and thin by a medium amount, while Anek Latin holds nearly flat lines and lowercase that climbs close to the capitals.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-anek-malayalam: Commanding up top, Quilon keeps its thick stems and hairlines in a close ratio. Anek Malayalam, a clean sans, hardly varies at all, and its curves stop short of touching, which gives the lowercase a light, uncrowded feel.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-anek-odia: Anek Odia is a clean, contemporary sans whose rounds stay unsealed, like a hook left unlatched, under Quilon's display strokes. Paragraphs move along easily.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-anek-tamil: Anek Tamil reads big and round, its bowls full. Quilon's soft, hand-inked modulation set against that plain sans is the pair's best quality, a gentle push and pull between pen and geometry.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-anek-telugu: Anek Telugu reads in wide, tall bowls, its rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook. And Quilon, with its flat-brush, half-turned contrast, gives that plain sans a heading with some grain to it.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-anuphan: Quilon sets an editorial tone, its thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones. And Anuphan follows in big round bowls with clear gaps, a sans that moves through paragraphs without catching.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-arimo: Soft ink, firm voice. Quilon swells like a worn felt marker, and Arimo, with its tall mean line and spacious gaps in the rounds, gives that sense of confidence a level place to land.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-armata: Quilon carries gently modulated strokes with no sharp hairlines. If it were made small, though, Armata would hold up better, since its lowercase fills most of the letter height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-athiti: Athiti draws each bowl at a single line width, like vinyl cut in a sign shop. Quilon adds a modest thick-thin swing on top, so the headings feel handled and the text feels precise.
